title: Two-term determinant and kernel data in the arrow category of modules
statement: Let $R$ be a commutative ring. Encode a cochain complex of $R$-modules concentrated in degrees $-1,0$ [def-weil-abstract-derived-category] by an arrow $d_P:P^{-1}\to P^0$ in the category of $R$-modules, and a chain map $a:P\to Q$ by a commuting square $a^0d_P=d_Qa^{-1}$. Such a map is degreewise surjective when both components are surjective. Its map on degree-minus-one cohomology is the restriction $\ker d_P\to\ker d_Q$ of $a^{-1}$, and it is a quasi-isomorphism when this restriction and the induced map $P^0/\operatorname{im}d_P\to Q^0/\operatorname{im}d_Q$ are bijective. Write $\det_R(V)$ for the exterior-socle determinant module [def-trf-projective-determinant-module]. Using tensor products [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product] and $V^\vee=\operatorname{Hom}_R(V,R)$, put $D(P)=\det_R(P^0)\otimes_R\det_R(P^{-1})^\vee$. Define $d_N:\ker a^{-1}\to\ker a^0$ by restriction of $d_P$, and put $D(N)=\det_R(\ker a^0)\otimes_R\det_R(\ker a^{-1})^\vee$. These definitions do not require any finite projectivity or quasi-isomorphism hypothesis.
